method.summary: Two independent denominators are scored row by row. Full V3 uses 100 weight points spread over the 14 workstreams; W07 is expanded into 12 lane rows weighted by capability count (30 points over 103 capabilities), W08 into 4 route rows (2 points each), and the 4 exclusions get 0.5 points each. Formal core uses 140 units: 103 capability units (one per capability, grouped in 12 lane rows), 4 routes at 3 units each, and 25 units for five cross-cutting formal obligations. Each lane row's low/central/high is the arithmetic mean of its capability entries; capability lows and highs are derived deterministically from the central value and an evidence-class band. Percent = 100 * sum(weight*score) / sum(weight).

full_v3.w07_rule: lane weight = 30 * capability_count / 103 (ASSET_TRANSFER 2.0388, SPOT 2.9126, FARM 1.7476, ZDEX 2.0388, ZUSD 3.7864, PERPS 3.2039, ORACLE 2.9126, SEALED 2.9126, STRATEGY 2.0388, PROOF 1.7476, EXTERNAL 2.6214, GOVERNANCE 2.0388)

method.interval_meaning: lower/central/upper are judgment and coverage intervals: the central value is the reviewer's best estimate from source inspection; lower is what remains defensible if every historical or uninspected claim is discounted per the band rule; upper is what could be true if all recorded but unreplayed evidence holds. They are not statistical confidence intervals and do not estimate hours or effort remaining.
method.weights_rationale: Weights follow the plan's own emphasis: the twelve-lane functional core (W07 30) plus refinement (W09 10) form the stated objective; publication/verification shell rows (W03-W06, W10, W11) total 29 because production value safety is the third milestone; discovery/semantics rows (W00-W02) total 11; release assessment and product (W12, W13) total 10 because they cannot start before the others close. Moving 10 points from the shell rows (mean score about 0.35) to W07 (score 0.145) lowers the full-V3 central by about 2 points; the estimate is more sensitive to how legacy donors are credited (see sensitivities).
method.overlap_and_double_counting: W07 lane rows credit semantics, implementation, lifecycle-path coverage and per-command proofs of that lane. W09 credits only the cross-lane refinement infrastructure (universal codec/parser correspondence, Python/Rust execution refinement, trace composition, ESSO/Kani), so per-lane proofs are not counted twice. W04 credits allocation derivation as a shell obligation; the formal core counts the allocation relation once under F-ALLOC. W03/W06/W10/W11 are release-qualification obligations and are excluded from the formal-core denominator entirely.

sensitivities.legacy_donor_zero: If legacy-only capabilities (flagged legacy_only) are credited only the 0.03 baseline, full V3 central falls to about 21.7 and formal core central to about 15.4. This is the largest single judgment in the estimate.
sensitivities.unknown_as_low: If rows whose evidence is entirely historical, unknown or absent (W10, W13) are scored at their lower band, full V3 central falls to about 22.3; formal core is unchanged because every formal row has at least one inspected Lean or Python source.
sensitivities.weight_shift: Shifting 10 points from W03-W06/W10/W11 to W07 lowers full V3 central by about 2 points; the formal-core figure does not depend on those weights.

anti_gaming: Fixed denominator: 14 workstreams, 12 lanes, 103 capabilities, 4 routes, 4 exclusions pinned to the plan hash. Newly discovered obligations expand the denominator; nothing is removed. A capability may only be split or merged by a superseding record that restates every affected row; until each part has its own evidence, a split part inherits the minimum of its parents' scores.

Completed notes earn nothing: checklist ticks, support records, test counts, packet counts and commit counts are not inputs. Credit moves only when a cited evidence path exists in the assessed snapshot and names the acceptance check it satisfies. A row above 0.20 must cite at least one VERIFIED non-documentation path unless it is a documentation workstream (docs_only_allowed).
Disabled or policy-blocked capabilities are capped at 0.15 in both denominators; a fail-closed reject is one lifecycle path, not a feature.

Historical drift: evidence bound to another commit is HISTORICAL and takes the wider band; if the owning source hash changed since that record, the evidence is STALE and is excluded from verified evidence (calculator treats STALE like UNKNOWN).
Missing evidence is never rounded up: UNKNOWN uses low = central/2 and its weight share is reported separately.

Correlated reviewer error: two assessors score independently; agreement does not raise a score. A disagreement above 0.15 on a row is resolved only by the acceptance evidence, otherwise the lower value stands. Any row at or above 0.95 requires external_review_accepted bound to the EXTERNAL_MAINTAINER_OR_CI_PREMISE already used by tools/check_v3_progress.py. Model agreement alone never authorizes completion.

Rate-of-change rule for re-assessment: compare to the prior assessment's rows; a score may rise only with a newly cited evidence path or a newly closed acceptance check; report closed, narrowed, regressed and newly discovered obligations separately, as the plan already requires.
Weights and ladders are frozen in this method version; a change requires a superseding method version reporting both old and new totals.

Weights and ladders are judgment; the sensitivities section quantifies the two largest choices (legacy donor credit and shell-versus-lane weighting).
Intervals are coverage bands, not statistical confidence intervals, and say nothing about effort or hours remaining.
Prior percentage estimates and prior reviewer commentary were not used as anchors; agreement with any other assessor must not be read as confirmation.
